title: ALL CAPS: THE HISTORY OF THE AMERICAN BASEBALL HAT
chaptersLine: Forty-plus chapters drafted, plus an introduction and a closing coda.
spanLine: From before the Civil War to the drops of 2026.
thisWeek: Recorded a second sit-down with a trade veteran already in the book, going deeper than the first conversation.
Closed a long-standing question about the one season a legendary franchise traded away its signature color, and folded the settled version into the draft.
A first-person writing pass built out the Los Angeles chapter around a shop that has held the same boulevard address for twenty years.
chapterHighlights: A 1996 World Series phone call that changed who a team's cap was allowed to belong to.
The Brooklyn crew who claimed a preppy luxury label and rewrote who a brand belongs to.
How a 1920 Buffalo startup ended up on nearly every professional cap on the field.
An East Los Angeles boulevard where the right cap has always been a form of belonging.
